advances: Uses actual equal-spacing section centroids and common cap mass on one three-fiber chain. The summed formal optimum and realized middle hemisphere are separate quantities, and the criterion is for the weighted cap response of this field.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The midpoint inclusion makes the prescribed lifted hull compatible: combinations at zero use equal endpoint weights, while the two endpoint bases are exposed. The base component of each section centroid gives $\sigma_{j,-1}=\sigma_{j,1}$, since the coarea factor for that cap is the same at all bases. Therefore $T_{-1}=T_1=T$. The circuit normalization gives $\sum_zT_z=\sum_j\theta_jS_jv_j=0$ and hence $T_0=-2T$. Using $b_j=v_j\cdot y$, the same two identities give
$$
\sum_z B_z=\sum_j\theta_j\left(S_jb_j-a_j\sum_z z\sigma_{jz}\right)=0 .
$$
Also $\sum_z C_z=Q$ because the cap weights sum to one and every cap has mass $Q$.

On a proper trace, apply the divergence theorem to $x-c$ on the clipped fiber. The new flat face has outward normal $-v_j/\lVert v_j\rVert$ and flux $-(b_j-a_jz-v_j\cdot c)\sigma_{jz}$. Thus the remaining flux on the original boundary is $d|K_z\cap(H_j)_z|+(b_j-a_jz-v_j\cdot c)\sigma_{jz}$. Strictly saturated traces and surface-null supporting traces have zero cutting-face contribution and give the same identity. In dimension one it is subtraction of endpoint fluxes on an interval. Summing with the weights gives $dC_z+B_z-T_z\cdot c$; its maximum over $K_z$ is the support formula. Fact 20c10d02dc799a5b realizes it by a continuous convex normal hinge with an affine penalty vanishing at the chosen exposed endpoint and strictly negative at the other two bases, chosen large enough to suppress their entire boundary. It is an actual erosion by the roof realization in 340f949c484a612f. Summing the support values uses $h_A(-T)+h_B(-T)=2h_{M_0}(-T)$ and $h_K(2T)=2h_K(T)$, proving the formal sum. Midpoint containment implies $h_K(T)\ge h_{M_0}(T)$, and $M_0$ has positive width in every nonzero direction.

The support choices give $m\in M_0\subseteq K$ and $T\cdot D=G$. The lifted triangle with vertices $(-1,p),(0,r),(1,q)$ lies inside the body. Its section at base $z\in[-1,1]$ is the segment from $f(z)$ to $f(z)+(1-|z|)D$, so its support in direction $n$ is $n\cdot f(z)+(1-|z|)(n\cdot D)_+$. This is concave in $z$, including on the global extension using the same formula. Therefore $\Phi$ is jointly continuous, nonnegative, globally finite and convex in $(z,x)$ for fixed $n$. Fact 340f949c484a612f realizes it as the actual inward normal speed on the measured boundaries. On each measured boundary with outward normal $n$, the bracket before taking the positive part is nonnegative because the center section lies inside its fiber. Thus the endpoint speeds are radial about $p,q$, and the middle speed is the affine-center radial speed about $m$ minus $(n\cdot D)_+$.

The sum of unweighted affine-center radial integrals about $f(z)$ is $dV$ by the divergence theorem. Their $W$-weighted sum is $dQ$ by the clipped-fiber identity: the $B_z$ sum vanishes, and $\sum_z T_z\cdot f(z)=0$ because $\sum_zT_z=0$ and $T_{-1}=T_1$. Subtracting the middle correction proves $dV-J$ and $dQ-L_+$. The denominator is positive since the two endpoint contributions are $d(|A|+|B|)>0$ and the middle speed is nonnegative. Applying the divergence theorem to constant vector fields on each clipped middle trace gives $\int_{\partial K}Wn\,dS=T_0=-2T$. Pair with $D$ and use $(n\cdot D)_+-(-n\cdot D)_+=n\cdot D$ to get $L_--L_+=2T\cdot D=2G$. Multiplying the proposed ratio bound by its positive denominator gives the last criterion.
statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $K_{-1}=A,K_0=K,K_1=B$ be positive convex fibers at the complete bases $-1,0,1$, with $M_0=(A+B)/2\subseteq K$ and $V=|A|+|K|+|B|$. Let a finite regular positive circuit have caps $H_j=\{a_jz+v_j\cdot x\ge b_j\}$ with $v_j\ne0$, $b_j=v_j\cdot y$, common raw mixed cap mass $Q$, and $\sum_j\rho_jv_j=0$ with $\rho_j>0$. Assume each cutting plane has positive full mixed section measure and centroid $(0,y)$ under the summed section measure on the fibers, and each fiber's boundary intersection with the plane is surface-null. This allows proper, strictly full and strictly empty traces. At base $z$ write
$$
\sigma_{jz}=\frac{\mathcal H^{d-1}(K_z\cap\{v_j\cdot x=b_j-a_jz\})}{\lVert v_j\rVert},
\quad S_j=\sum_z\sigma_{jz},
\quad \theta_j=\frac{\rho_j/S_j}{\sum_\ell\rho_\ell/S_\ell},
\quad W=\sum_j\theta_j\mathbf1_{H_j}.
$$
Set $C_z=\sum_j\theta_j|K_z\cap(H_j)_z|$, $T_z=\sum_j\theta_j\sigma_{jz}v_j$ and $B_z=\sum_j\theta_j\sigma_{jz}(b_j-a_jz)$. Then $T_{-1}=T_1=T$, $T_0=-2T$ and $\sum_z B_z=0$. For each fiber the best numerator over radial centers in that fiber is
$$
F_z=\max_{c\in K_z}\int_{\partial K_z}W\,n\cdot(x-c)\,dS
=dC_z+B_z+h_{K_z}(-T_z).
$$
The two endpoint optima are each realized by an actual normal-dependent erosion supported on that base. The independent-fiber formal sum is
$$
\sum_z F_z=dQ+2G,\qquad
G=h_{M_0}(-T)+h_K(T)\ge h_{M_0}(-T)+h_{M_0}(T),
$$
so $G>0$ when $T\ne0$.

Choose $p\in A,q\in B$ minimizing $T\cdot x$ in their respective fibers, $r\in K$ maximizing it, and put $m=(p+q)/2$, $D=r-m$, $f(z)=m+z(q-p)/2$. For each unit $n$ define
$$
\Phi(n,z,x)=\big[n\cdot(x-f(z))-(1-|z|)(n\cdot D)_+\big]_+ .
$$
This is the actual inward speed of a compatible convex roof erosion. Put $J=\int_{\partial K}(n\cdot D)_+\,dS$ and $L_\pm=\int_{\partial K}(\pm n\cdot D)_+W\,dS$. The total and weighted boundary integrals of $\Phi$ over all three measured fibers are respectively $dV-J>0$ and $dQ-L_+$, with
$$
L_--L_+=2G.
$$
Thus the weighted-to-total ratio is at least $\gamma$ exactly when $\gamma J-L_+\ge d(\gamma V-Q)$.
title: Exact three-fiber support gain and an actual center-triangle erosion
